title: The Trump Economy Is Starting To BOOM
summary: Podcast arguing the economy is booming under Trump: inflation at a five-year low, real wage growth, strong jobs and GDP, and the tariff price warnings proved wrong.

assertions.quote: the CPI as the lowest we've had in five years

verdicts.note: January 2026 CPI of 2.4% was the lowest since 2021 and below the long-run average, but still above the Fed's 2% target.

Headline CPI was 2.4% in January 2026, tied for the lowest reading since February 2021 (2.3% in April 2025), far below the 9.1% peak of June 2022 and about the 2019-20 pre-pandemic pace (2.3-2.5%); it remained above the 2% target, and the series only spans 2019-2026.

assertions.quote: wage growth outpaced inflation, meaning there was actual real wage growth this past year

verdicts.note: Average hourly earnings rose about 3.7% against CPI of 2.4% in the year to January 2026.
Derived real average hourly earnings rose 1.2% in the 12 months to January 2026 (nominal AHE +3.7% vs CPI +2.4%).

assertions.quote: That never happened under the Biden administration.

verdicts.note: Real average hourly earnings fell in 2021-22 but rose in 2023 and 2024 as inflation dropped below wage growth.

Derived real average hourly earnings growth was positive every month from May 2023 through January 2025, including +0.8% in December 2023 and +1.2% in December 2024, so real wages grew in 2023 and 2024 after falling in 2021-22.

assertions.quote: Prices have not increased at all. In fact, inflation, the rate has actually gone down, not up, even since the tariffs were implemented.
the rate has actually gone down, not up, even since the tariffs were implemented

verdicts.note: Headline CPI fell from 3.0% in January 2025 to about 2.4% in January 2026, though goods prices rose in tariffed categories.

Headline CPI fell from 3.0% in January 2025 (2.8% in February) to 2.4% in January 2026 and core from 3.3% to 2.5%, though headline dipped to 2.3% in April 2025 and rebounded to 3.0% by September 2025 before easing; the series settle the direction of the rate, not any causal role of tariffs.

assertions.quote: prices are technically expanding, but the actual rate is decreasing

verdicts.note: From January 2023 to September 2024 the 12-month inflation rate fell from 6.4% to 2.4% while the CPI-U level rose from 299.17 to 315.301; a falling rate means prices rise more slowly, not that they fall.

assertions.quote: the only times prices will actually decrease is if you have a recession or a depression

verdicts.note: Broad deflation has accompanied severe downturns, but prices also dipped briefly in 2015 on an oil crash without a recession.

Single-month declines in the all-items index occur outside recessions (seasonally adjusted -0.4% in June 2026; unadjusted declines in late 2022 and late 2023), but in 2019-2026 the 12-month change never went negative, not even in the 2020 recession (low of 0.1% in May 2020), so sustained outright deflation did not occur in any condition covered.

assertions.quote: Gas prices are down, egg prices are dramatically down.

verdicts.note: Egg prices fell sharply from the 2025 bird-flu peak and gasoline averaged lower in 2025 than in 2024, before the Iran war.

The gasoline half holds for early 2026: Jan and Feb 2026 regular gasoline (2.809, 2.908) were 8.7% and 5.5% below the January 2025 inauguration-month price of 3.076, though the gap vanished in March 2026 (3.638); the egg half is outside this series.
